title: Kestrel and the Wreck
premise: Salvage diver Rafael Thornbury takes a dying prospector's river map in exchange for a promise to deliver it upstream, and discovers it charts the source of the very wreck the navy has spent three years keeping him away from. Following the Kestrel River into forbidden highlands with a runaway cartographer and the prospector's estranged daughter, Rafael uncovers a sunken inheritance his own family helped bury — and learns the navy's silence protects a crime, not a secret. When the expedition's loyalty fractures over what to do with the truth, Rafael must choose between keeping his promise to a dead man and exposing the wreck that has defined his life. In the end he surfaces the evidence, loses the river but gains a family, and finally stops measuring his life in miles.
about_author: Noor Ishikawa is a former marine surveyor who traded sonar readouts for sentences and now writes adventure fiction from a houseboat on a slow northern river. Kestrel and the Wreck is her third novel and her first to draw directly on years spent mapping waterways no one was supposed to question.

chapters.title: Three Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Diving a wrecked naval transport the navy forbids him to photograph, Rafael counts air tanks and river miles instead of birthdays, grieving the brother lost aboard. When a navy patrol nearly catches him salvaging an unlogged hull plate, he pockets it anyway. Emotional beat: restless defiance — a man who has stopped believing answers will ever come to him.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A feverish old prospector named Aldous Wren collapses at Rafael's dock and trades a hand-drawn map of the Kestrel's source for one promise: carry it upstream before the navy finds it. Wren dies by dawn, whispering that the wreck 'wasn't an accident.' Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance — Rafael accepts a debt to a stranger because no one ever made one to him.

chapters.title: What the Plate Says
chapters.summary: Alternating Rafael and Mara POV. Mara Wren, the prospector's estranged daughter and a disgraced naval cartographer, arrives hunting her father's map. Instead she deciphers Rafael's hull plate: a serial matching a ship officially scrapped decades before the wreck. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance — two people who distrust each other more than the navy, bound by the same dead man.

chapters.title: Upstream, Uninvited
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The pair slips past a checkpoint using Mara's old credentials, joined by Ferro, a river pilot who owes Rafael his life. The map shows rapids that appear on no chart, and a navy cutter begins shadowing them. Emotional beat: fragile momentum — the found family forms around shared secrets before shared trust.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A reservoir behind an old dam swallows a village the maps still claim exists. Diving it, Rafael finds the transport's sister ship — scuttled deliberately, cargo holds full of sealed crates. Ferro recognizes the dam's builder: Rafael's grandfather. Emotional beat: vertigo of lineage — the inheritance theme turns personal and poisonous.

chapters.title: Ferro's Price
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Navy officers intercept the boat and offer Ferro amnesty for the map. Torn between the debt he owes Rafael and a daughter he hasn't seen in years, Ferro leads the cutter astray but burns his own escape route doing it. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and paid for — the first real cost of the journey.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Above the dam, the river's true source is a flooded mine shaft where the crates originated: smuggled gold moved under naval escort, the transport sunk to erase the ledger. Mara finds her father's final survey notes — he'd been the navy's cartographer on the cover-up. Emotional beat: grief braided with revelation — truth and betrayal share a bloodline.

chapters.title: Broken Compass
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The cutter corners them at the mine; the commander reveals Rafael's brother died trying to report the same cargo, and the navy offers Rafael his brother's sealed file in exchange for the map and silence. Mara accuses Rafael of considering it. Emotional beat: the fracture — loyalty to the dead, to the living, and to truth pull in three directions at once.

chapters.title: The Ledger Surfaces
chapters.summary: Rafael and Mara's POV, alternating. Rafael refuses the bargain; Ferro rams the cutter in a sacrificial run that lets Rafael raise the cargo manifest from the mine's flooded gallery. Wounded, they drift downstream through the dam's spillway with the evidence as the navy closes in. Emotional beat: climax — the promise kept at nearly fatal cost, truth chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Miles, No Longer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, epilogue-flavored. The manifest reaches a journalist; inquiries begin, and Rafael's brother is posthumously cleared. Ferro survives, reunited with his daughter; Mara redraws the maps with the village's true name restored. Rafael dives the wreck one last time — not to salvage, but to say goodbye. Emotional beat: resolution — he inherits not gold but a family, and measures his life in years again.
